name: Kisspeptin restart

card.summary: An experimental peptide-based approach some use after testosterone or steroid use to try to restart the body's own hormone signalling, aimed at keeping muscle, skin and physique gains.
card.note: Kisspeptin is a research peptide; human studies have been short-term and not for recovery after steroid use.

quick.overview:
Kisspeptin restart refers to using kisspeptin, a hypothalamic peptide that drives the signal for the pituitary to release LH and FSH, as an experimental way to restart the hormone axis after suppression from testosterone or other androgens. The appearance link is the chain testosterone recovery, then retained muscle, body composition and skin or hair effects tied to androgen status.

Kisspeptin was discovered in 1996 as a melanoma metastasis suppressor and shown in 2003 to be essential for puberty. Clinical trials have given it briefly to healthy volunteers and patients with reproductive disorders and found it raises LH, but no trial has tested it as post-cycle therapy.
quick.how: Forum members describe it as an injected research peptide used in place of or alongside hCG, clomiphene or similar products, sometimes during ongoing TRT. Dose and sourcing details are not covered here.
quick.risks: It is not an approved drug. Reported human trials are short, and safety, purity of gray-market products and long-term effects on the axis are not established.

lead: Kisspeptin restart, sometimes called kisspeptin PCT, is a community term for using kisspeptin peptides (commonly kisspeptin-10) to try to reactivate the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis after it has been suppressed by exogenous testosterone or anabolic steroids. [1][2]

The appearance chain is indirect: if the axis recovers, a person's own testosterone production returns, which users hope will help them keep muscle, body composition and other androgen-dependent features after finishing a cycle or in place of hCG while on TRT. [2]

Kisspeptins are encoded by the KISS1 gene and act on the GPR54 (Kiss1R) receptor on GnRH neurons, which triggers GnRH and then LH and FSH release. Wikipedia notes the gene was identified in 1996 and linked to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in 2003. [1] No published trial has tested kisspeptin as a post-cycle recovery agent.

angle.text: Users describe it as a way to keep the pituitary-gonadal signal alive during or after androgen use so physique and related traits are maintained. The route from kisspeptin to those outcomes has not been tested in recovery studies.

paras: Kisspeptin neurons in the hypothalamus act as a central regulator of the reproductive axis, integrating metabolic and steroid-feedback signals and gating GnRH release. [3][4] Energy balance and stress affect kisspeptin signalling, and a review links stress-related suppression of this system with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea in women. [5][3]

Kisspeptin was identified in 1996 in Danny Welch's lab in Hershey, Pennsylvania as a metastasis suppressor. The receptor was cloned in 1999-2001, and in 2003 receptor mutations were tied to failure of puberty. [1]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and TRT communities
paras: On T Nation, members mention kisspeptin-10 as a possible substitute for hCG, with one poster saying it may avoid desensitization seen with other agents. [6] Others describe adding it to a clomiphene regimen or TRT. [7][8] These are self-reports; no controlled data accompany them.

Randomized trials in healthy men and women show kisspeptin administration raises gonadotropin levels, including a 2025 trial of intranasal kisspeptin and a 2025 trial finding no effect on anxiety. [9][10] A 2013 study found a single kisspeptin-54 injection temporarily increased LH pulsatility in healthy women, and a 2022 trial examined bone metabolism in healthy men. [11][12] Registered trials have looked at hypothalamic amenorrhea, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and IVF. [13][14] None has examined recovery after steroid or testosterone use.

timeline.event: KISS1 identified as a metastasis suppressor. [1]
Kisspeptin receptor mutations linked to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. [1]

lore.intro: Kisspeptin appears on T Nation threads about TRT and recovery as an alternative to hCG. [6][7]

claims.claim: Kisspeptin-10 can stand in for hCG to keep the testes active on TRT
claims.believers: Posters say it may provide similar value with less desensitization and describe it as keeping testes active, though not optimal. [6][7]
claims.experts: Trials show kisspeptin raises LH in volunteers over short periods, but none has compared it with hCG on TRT. [9][11]
